diffs.diff: minimum supply: part 3 V, datasheet reading 4.5 V
diffs.evidence: 4.5 V (Typ 5.0, Min 4.5, Max 5.5) is the bare Plantower sensor's 'DC Power Supply' rating, i.e. the sensor's own 5 V pins. The model is the Soldered 333058 adapter, whose header VCC is not the sensor supply: the vendor schematic (V1.1.1) shows a block titled 'BOOST CONVERTER 3V3>>5V' where header VCC feeds L1 (2.2 uH) into the SW pin of U1 TPS613222A, whose VOUT net '5V' feeds the sensor connector's VCC pins; the vendor pinout sheet says 'VCC: 3.3V' and 'Be careful, 3.3V voltage level'. TI TPS61322 datasheet: 'Operating input voltage range: 0.9 V to 5.5 V'; TPS613222A VOUT 4.85-5.15 V; 'The TPS613222A can support as high as 500-mA output current from 3-V input voltage to 5-V output voltage conversion', well above the sensor's <=100 mA. So 3.0-5.5 V at the adapter VCC is correct, and the model already states the bare sensor needs 4.5-5.5 V.

diffs.diff: PM1.0 concentration (ug/m3): datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: Plantower PMS7003 data manual V2.5, Technical Index: 'Resolution 1 ug/m3'; Appendix I frame table: 'Data4 refers to PM1.0 concentration unit ug/m3 (under atmospheric environment)', 'Data 5 refers to PM2.5 concentration unit ug/m3', 'Data 6 refers to concentration unit (under atmospheric environment) ug/m3' (Data1-3 the same for CF=1). So each count of the 16-bit word is 1 ug/m3, offset 0. The model already uses exactly this: sim.uartStream encodes pm1/value/pm10 as 16-bit words with scale 1 (offset 0), and the driver returns the raw words as ug/m3. The gate reports 'none' only because its conversion extractor reads sim.measure/measures/responses and not sim.uartStream, so it does not see the model's scale-1 encoding.
